newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JUNE 3.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
--The finance ministry's draft bill on the reduction of tax fines will reduce fines by around 50 percent although the issuing of bogus receipts and invoices will continue to be dealt with severely.

--The EFTE charge on drachma loans will fall from 4-3 percent and also be applied to forex loans, according to an amendment brought to a parliamentary committee by the national economy ministry. The measure is expected to make drachma lending more attractive than forex, which accounts for 38 percent of total loans.
--The government indicated yesterday that there would be no slackening of economic policy and was examining additional measures, despite the win of the French Left in elections over the weekend.
--The positions of 15 general secretaries at ministries will be abolished if Cabinet approves yesterday's decision from a committee studying the restructuring of the public sector.

--Public revenues were up by 22.9 percent in May, according to initial estimates from the finance ministry. The ministry says it is relatively satisfied with the course of public infolws and Dpeuty Finance Minister George Drys said it confirmed the ministry's predictions that the tide would turn as of May.

--Investments of 31 billion drachmas for 86 investment plans for Eastern Macedonia and Thrace were approved for first half 1997. The investments are concentrated in the foodstuffs and textiles sectors.
--The finance ministry's new regional control centres - to conduct checks on companies with annual before tax income of 350 million drachmas - will be in place by September.
--The Athens Stock Exchange overcame initial downward trends at the beginning of trading yesterday to close up by 1.08 percent at 1,652.99 points.
